subject: general
question: A train of length 490 m overtakes a man moving at a speed of 9 km/hr (in the same direction) in 12 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take this train to completely cross another train that has is 500 m long, moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 42 km/hr?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (Train 1 & Man) = 490 / 12 m/s = (490 / 12) × (18 / 5) = 147 km/hr.

Speed of Train 1 = 147 + 9 = 156 km/hr.

Relative speed (Train 1 & Train 2) = 156 + 42 = 198 km/hr = 198 × (5 / 18) = 55 m/s.

Time to cross = Total Length ÷ Relative speed = (490 + 500) / 55 = 18 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of Train 1 (L₁) = 490 m

Speed of Man = 9 km/hr

Time to overtake man = 12 s

Length of Train 2 (L₂) = 500 m

Speed of Train 2 = 42 km/hr

 Total Crossing Distance = 490 + 500 = 990 m

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

When moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = v₁ − v₂

When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = v₁ + v₂

To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed of Train 1 and Man = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ v₁ − 9 = (490 / 12) m/s

⇒ v₁ − 9 = (490 / 12) × (18 / 5) km/hr

⇒ v₁ − 9 = 490 × 18 / 60 = 147 km/hr

⇒ v₁ = 147 + 9 = 156 km/hr

⇒ Relative speed with Train 2 (opposite direction) = v₁ + v₂

⇒ Relative speed = 156 + 42 = 198 km/hr

⇒ Speed in m/s = 198 × (5 / 18) = 55 m/s

⇒ Total distance to cross = L₁ + L₂ = 490 + 500 = 990 m

⇒ Time taken = Total distance ÷ Relative speed in m/s

⇒ Time = 990 / 55 = 18 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 18 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (v₁ + v₂).

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (v₁ − v₂).

Train Crossing an Object

Time taken to cross a stationary point object like a pole = Length of train ÷ Speed of train.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.
